task.title: Relics: benchmark relics and confirm the limits
task.description:
A relic is a new kind of record in Workbook, separate from tasks. It holds specs, plans, decisions, transcripts and similar material, with the same history and sharing that tasks have. A relic has a title, a type, an author, links, and content made of named parts.

This story adds a relic family to the existing benchmark harness and proves the design is fast enough. It is part of the first working version on purpose: speed has to be known, and keep being measurable, before any further relic feature is built. Every later relic story waits for this one.

## What is measured

| Measured | At this size |
| --- | --- |
| Create a relic, edit one part, open a relic | A 2,000-part relic holding 1 MiB of text |
| Read one body from the command line | A 1 MiB body and a 2 KiB body |
| List relics, filter by type | 1,000 relics of 20 parts each |
| Find everything that links to one part or task | 10,000 links |
| Reorder parts heavily, and report the longest position | 2,000 parts, 10,000 moves |
| Sync changed relics | 100 changed relics |
| Rebuild the index, and fetch into a fresh clone | The full set above |
| Storage growth | Repository size before and after the edits above |
| Task commands with relics present | The existing task scenarios, re-run beside 1,000 relics |

Reports stay descriptive, with no pass or fail inside the harness, as they are for tasks.

## Targets this story must meet

- Once the index exists, "which relics link to this one?" is answered from the index alone, without reading Git.
- On a fresh clone, building the index for the full set (1,000 relics, 20,000 parts, 10,000 links) takes under 5 seconds on the benchmark machine. It must never take minutes.
- After a sync, only the relics that changed are re-read, so the cost follows the size of the change and not the size of the project.
- Task commands are not measurably slower with 1,000 relics present.

If a target is missed, fix the cause in this story. If the 5-second figure turns out to be the wrong number for a good reason, say so with the measurements and ask Dylan before changing it.

## Decisions this story makes with data

- **Starting limits.** Confirm each starting size limit or raise it. Limits can be raised and never lowered, so only raise one that the measurements support.
- **Body caching.** Bodies are not cached today. If reading a body from the command line is slow, copy bodies under a size threshold into the index. The web server may also keep recently shown bodies in memory, since an object ID always means the same text.
- **Renumbering parts.** Positions use the shortest fraction that fits and are limited to 256 bytes. If the heavy reorder scenario shows real use can reach the limit, add a "renumber parts" change that resets every position to a whole number in one recorded change, and document what happens to a move made at the same moment.

## Done when

- The relic scenarios run from the existing harness and their report is stored where task reports are.
- Every target above is met, or Dylan has agreed a different figure.
- The three decisions above are made and written into the reference and architecture documents.
- The benchmark can be re-run after each later relic story with one command.

## Not in this story

History and diff timings, which the history and diffs story measures when it adds those commands.

## Where the design is

The approved design is "Workbook Relics Design" (2026-11-21). It is kept out of the repository. Until "Relics: teach agents to use relics and store the design as the first relic" is done, an untracked copy sits at `specs/2026-11-21-relics-design.html` in Dylan's checkout. After that, read the relic. This description carries what the story needs, and the design wins where the two disagree.
